claim: The node or shard limit per cluster can be increased to a maximum of 500 if the engine version is Valkey 7.2 and higher, or Redis OSS 5.0.6 to 7.1. For example, a 500 node cluster can range between 83 shards (one primary and 5 replicas per shard) and 500 shards (single primary and no replicas).

values.spoken: a maximum of five hundred per cluster

qualifiers.scope: per Valkey or Redis OSS cluster
qualifiers.condition: Valkey 7.2 and higher, or Redis OSS 5.0.6 to 7.1; needs enough free IP addresses in the subnet group

evidence.quote: The node or shard limit can be increased to a maximum of 500 per cluster if the engine version is Valkey 7.2 and higher, or Redis OSS 5.0.6 to 7.1. For example, you can choose to configure a 500 node cluster that ranges between 83 shards (one primary and 5 replicas per shard) and 500 shards (single primary and no replicas).

note: The NodeGroups page words the engine condition as Valkey or Redis OSS 5.0.6 or higher; the Shards page is the more specific one and is used here.

claim: If Multi-AZ is enabled, a failed primary node fails over to the replica with the least replication lag. The replica is promoted automatically, and this usually takes just a few seconds until you can write to the cluster again.
question: How long does a Multi-AZ automatic failover usually take, and which replica becomes the primary?

values.display: the replica with the least replication lag
values.spoken: the replica with the least replication lag

qualifiers.scope: per Valkey or Redis OSS replication group with Multi-AZ enabled
qualifiers.condition: Multi-AZ enabled; the primary node fails

evidence.quote: If you enable Multi-AZ, a failed primary node fails over to the replica with the least replication lag. The selected replica is automatically promoted to primary, which is much faster than creating and reprovisioning a new primary node. This process usually takes just a few seconds until you can write to the cluster again.

claim: On failover, ElastiCache flips the DNS record of the cache node to point at the read replica, which is promoted to become the new primary. A new healthy node joins the cluster within six minutes.

qualifiers.scope: per failover of a primary cache node
qualifiers.condition: the node synchronization time varies with workload and cluster size

evidence.quote: When failing over, ElastiCache flips the DNS record for your cache node to point at the read replica, which is in turn promoted to become the new primary. A new healthy node joins the cluster within six minutes.
